prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The monocular depth map shows a downward-angled outdoor view of a dirt path with patches of grass and a white rock about 1.2 to 1.5 metres below and in front of the camera wearer, while a brown-and-white dog stands directly below at roughly 0.5 to 1.0 metre distance across frames 1 to 4. In frames 2 to 4, the camera wearer's right arm and hand enter from the bottom right at about 0.3 to 0.6 metres away, reaching down within arm's reach to touch and partially occlude the dog's neck and collar while the dog faces left with its head nearer the camera than its hindquarters. In frame 5, as the camera turns rightward and shifts forward, the dog retreats to the bottom-left edge and is mostly out of view, while another person's lower legs, feet in pink footwear, and a dark strap or leash appear on the bottom right at roughly 0.6 to 1.2 metres distance, about 0.5 metres to the right of the dog. Compared to RGB alone, the depth map clearly separates the elevated foreground profiles of the reaching arm, the dog's torso, and the nearby person's legs (including the gap between their ankles) from the flat ground plane, and shows the ground sloping away toward the darker upper-left edge. However, the map is unreliable around the small rock on the path, which is flattened into the surrounding ground depth, and along the lower boundaries in frames 3 and 4 where the wearer's hand and the dog's back merge into a single bright depth region.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map sits on a black background that omits the dirt path, grass, and rock (1.2 to 1.5 metres away), isolating only portions of the foreground dog and the camera wearer's reaching arm at the bottom of frames 2 to 4 at roughly 0.3 to 1.0 metre distance. In frame 2, it separates the wearer's right arm on the bottom right (labelled 'person') from the dog's head on the bottom left (labelled 'dog') and hindquarters on the right, showing the arm within arm's reach overlapping and partially occluding the dog's upper back as the dog faces left away from the camera wearer. Across frames 1 to 5, the map is highly unreliable: it detects nothing in frame 1 despite the dog being clearly visible below the wearer, and detects nothing in frame 5 where the dog is partly out of view on the bottom left and the second person's legs stand 0.6 to 1.2 metres away on the bottom right. Furthermore, in frame 3 the dog and the wearer's hand are merged into a single pink mask mislabelled 'person', and in frame 4 the dog's body is misclassified as a 'donut' on the right and 'person' on the left while the wearer's hand is separately labelled 'person'. When masks do appear in frame 2, they help delineate the occlusion boundary where the wearer's forearm crosses over the dog's neck and collar, which blends somewhat in tone in the RGB image.
descriptions.pose: The body and hand skeleton map is completely black across all five frames, failing to detect any body or hand keypoints in the scene. In the RGB strip, the scene consists of a downward view onto a dirt path with a rock 1.2 to 1.5 metres ahead, a dog standing 0.5 to 1.0 metre below the camera wearer facing left (frames 1 to 4) before shifting to the bottom-left edge in frame 5, the camera wearer's own right forearm and hand reaching within arm's reach to touch the dog's collar in frames 2 to 4, and a second person's lower legs and feet appearing 0.6 to 1.2 metres away on the bottom right in frame 5. Because both the camera wearer and the second person are heavily cropped by the frame edges—leaving only a single bare arm in frames 2 to 4 and lower legs facing left/forward in frame 5 with heads and torsos completely out of view—neither person's gaze or full-body orientation is visible, and the pose estimator is completely unreliable under such extreme egocentric truncation. Consequently, the pose map provides no spatial information beyond what is in the RGB strip and fails to track the hand articulation on the dog's neck or the approaching step of the person on the right in frame 5.
